question:
A 35-year-old woman presents with a 3-month history of constipation, fatigue, muscle weakness,
polyuria, and polydipsia. Her medical history includes hypertension, managed with amlodipine 5 mg
daily, and bipolar disorder, treated with lithium 300 mg three times daily for the past 2 years. On
physical examination, her blood pressure is 141/75 mm Hg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and her
BMI is 32. Laboratory results include the following: | | Patient value | Reference range | | --- | --- | --- | |
Serum calcium (mg/dL) | 11.5 | 9.0–10.5 | | Albumin (g/dL) | 3.9 | 3.5–5.5 | | Phosphorus (mg/dL) | 2.5 |
3.0–4.5 | | Parathyroid hormone (pg/mL) | 85 | 10–60 | | 25-hydroxyvitamin D (ng/mL) | 31 | 30–80 | |
Magnesium (mg/dL) | 1.9 | 1.8–3.0 | Her serum calcium level was 9.8 mg/dL three years ago. A
complete blood count and results of electrolyte, kidney, and liver function tests are normal. What is the
most appropriate next step in managing this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Increase amlodipine dosage
(B) Order bone mineral density scan (C) Order nuclear imaging of the parathyroid glands (D) Initiate
treatment with cinacalcet (E) Begin treatment with bisphosphonates (F) Reduce lithium dosage by 50%
(G) Measure 24-hour urinary calcium excretion (H) Replace lithium with an alternative treatment for
bipolar disorder (I) Perform ultrasound of the parathyroid glands (J) Order genetic testing for MEN1
syndrome
 A. Reduce lithium dosage by 50%
B. Measure 24-hour urinary calcium excretion
C. Order bone mineral density scan
D. Order genetic testing for MEN1 syndrome
E. Increase amlodipine dosage
F. Perform ultrasound of the parathyroid glands
G. Begin treatment with bisphosphonates
H. Replace lithium with an alternative treatment for bipolar disorder
